title: Canonical functors for condensed lisse evaluation
statement: For a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], use its pulled-back coefficient [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and section-ring presentation. On a ringed site define A=O(U), F as exact constant realization [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] followed by the fixed universal derived coefficient extension [def-zl-derived-change-of-rings-model] and the section-module equivalence, and G as total right derived terminal evaluation. Define perfect objects [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], lisse objects as dualizable objects, and Statement as full faithfulness, triangulated strong symmetry, and the specified perfect/lisse equivalence with inverse G. On a profinite slice define the restricted coefficient, actual scalar homomorphism, and point-realization restriction using [def-zl-condensed-scalar-realization] and [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension]. For an affine scheme use the uniquely characterized relative test functor [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site] to define the actual inverse image, its coefficient-transported derived module functor, and the component/scalar comparison propositions. The component comparison section-ring isomorphism is normalized on point scalars: its composite with the actual profinite scalar map sends a scalar to the section obtained by monoidal point inverse image and evaluation on the sheafification-unit image of 1. This is the explicit affineScalarSection construction, also used by the projective calculus.
